rv.q: The dancers go at it with steamrolling energy, script and moves borrowing from the queer ballroom scene.
Club NVRLND achieves something very special - creating a party atmosphere where you can sing, dance and forget about the outside world from the moment that you walk through the door.
The show never gives up and will ensnare even the most cynical members of the audience when the party reaches its electrifying crescendo.
Whilst it certainly succeeds in delivering a thoroughly entertaining night out, it could benefit from a little refinement to ensure the theatrical experience is as compelling as the party itself.
It may not always succeed as a musical, but as a fully immersive party, it's difficult not to be swept along by the infectious sense of joy.
Club NVRLND doesn't take itself seriously for a single second, and that is precisely its superpower.
There’s nothing intrinsically special about this production, which is basically pretence (and maybe pretentiousness as well) to put on a rave themed after old-time hits.

cn.t: Critics find Club NVRLND a raucous, nostalgia-fueled good time that prioritizes 90s/00s party energy over plot. Most praise its infectious fun; skeptics say the thin narrative and gimmicky concept struggle to sustain a full show.
